prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and funding
- “Real change” for the many: tackle inequality, rebuild public services, and lead on climate action.
- Fair taxation: reverse some corporation tax cuts; higher income tax only above £80,000; major anti-avoidance drive; no VAT rise.
- End outsourcing and take PFI contracts back in-house; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, care homes and council housing; restore public-sector pay.

Green Industrial Revolution
- £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund), National Investment Bank and regional banks.
- Create 1m climate jobs; decarbonise power/heat (c.90% electricity, 50% heat from renewables by 2030).
- Build 7,000 offshore and 2,000 onshore wind turbines; mass solar; develop tidal and green hydrogen.
- Retrofit 27m homes; zero‑carbon homes standard; ban fracking; windfall tax on oil firms.
- Public ownership of energy networks/supply and water; delist firms that fail climate duties.

Transport and environment
- Rail and buses in public ownership; restore 3,000 bus routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils run services.
- Electrify rail; complete HS2 to Scotland; deliver Northern rail; boost cycling/walking; aim to end new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; expand EV charging.
- Clean Air Act, £5.6bn flood defences, tree planting, habitat recovery; producer responsibility for waste and bottle return; stronger animal welfare.

NHS and social care
- NHS funding up 4.3% a year; end privatisation; abolish prescription charges; free dental check-ups; capital investment (scanners, IT).
- Workforce bursaries; mental health parity with new standards and facilities.
- National Care Service: free personal care for older people; cap lifetime costs; better pay/conditions for care workers; higher Carer’s Allowance.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: free lifelong learning.
- Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; extend maternity leave to 12 months; recruit 150k early years staff.
- More school funding; max primary class size 30; scrap SATs; arts premium; bring academies/free schools under local democratic control; free school meals for all primary pupils.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; adult entitlements up to Level 3 and six years at Levels 4–6.

Work, rights and inequality
- Real Living Wage £10 for all 16+; rights from day one; ban zero‑hours; sectoral collective bargaining; Inclusive Ownership Funds (up to 10% employee stakes).
- Reduce average full‑time week to 32 hours within a decade (no loss of pay); new Ministry for Employment Rights; unified Workers’ Protection Agency.
- Corporate reform: worker‑elected directors (1/3 of boards), tougher takeover test, late‑payment crackdown, audit reform.

Housing and homelessness
- Build 1m+ social homes in a decade (150k/yr; 100k council); redefine “affordable” by incomes; end Right to Buy for council/HA homes.
- Private renting: rent caps, end no‑fault evictions, national licensing, renters’ unions; end leasehold abuses.
- Grenfell fire‑safety fund; end rough sleeping within five years (homes, services, local funding).

Justice, security and local power
- Rebuild neighbourhood policing (2,000 more officers than current plans); tackle violent and cybercrime; review Prevent.
- Reunify probation; presumption against short prison terms; restore legal aid; stronger action on VAWG.
- Reverse council cuts; insource services; revive high streets; Post Bank via a renationalised Royal Mail; national youth service.

Equalities, migration and welfare
- New Department for Women & Equalities; close gender pay gap by 2030; BAME pay-gap reporting; disability and LGBT+ rights strengthened.
- End hostile environment; scrap 2014 Immigration Act; end indefinite detention; close Yarl’s Wood/Brook House; safe routes for refugees.
- Replace DWP with Dept for Social Security; scrap Universal Credit; immediate fixes (end five‑week wait, sanctions, benefit cap and two‑child limit).

Constitution and Brexit
- Abolish House of Lords for an elected Senate (via Constitutional Convention); votes at 16; automatic registration; stronger lobbying/FOI rules.
- Brexit: negotiate a customs‑union/Single Market‑aligned deal and hold a binding referendum vs Remain within six months; automatic rights for EU citizens; implement result.

International and defence
- Human‑rights‑led foreign policy; suspend arms sales linked to abuses (Saudi in Yemen; Israel where used against civilians); recognise Palestine; War Powers Act.
- NATO, Trident renewal, spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; better pay, housing and support for forces and veterans.
- Keep DfID and 0.7% aid; make inequality a target; £4bn/yr international climate finance; end fossil‑fuel export support; trade tied to rights and standards.
